questions.sec: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma
questions.q: The alkyl group of alkylating agents is devoid of the ____ atom.
questions.exp: Alkyl group: devoid of 'H' atom (Book p282)

questions.sec: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma
questions.q: AA binds with the H atom on guanine at the ____ position.
questions.exp: AA bind with H atom on guanine (N7 position of guanine) (Book p282)

questions.sec: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma
questions.q: Guanine mispairing with thymidine produces which abnormal DNA pair?
questions.exp: Guanine mispairing with thymidine → G≡T abnormal DNA formation (Book p282)

questions.sec: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma
questions.q: If check gates are not functional, abnormal DNA proliferates → secondary carcinoma; the m/c secondary cancer (with platinum compounds & alkylating agents) is:
questions.exp: Secondary carcinoma: AML (m/c) — seen with platinum compound & alkylating agent (Book p282)

questions.q: Match the hepatic fate of cyclophosphamide to its consequence.
questions.exp: Phosphoramide mustard → cytotoxicity; acrolein → hemorrhagic cystitis (mesna); chloroacetaldehyde → neurotoxicity (GTCS, ataxia); inactive → excreted (Book p282)

questions.q: Prodrug cyclophosphamide's active form is ____.
questions.exp: Cyclophosphamide → 4-hydroxy cyclophosphamide (active) (Book p283)

questions.q: Match the cyclophosphamide use-group to its cancers.
questions.exp: Female: breast/ovary; kids: neuroblastoma, Wilms, ALL, NHL; DOC: Wegener's, steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome (Book p283)

questions.q: Ifosfamide (I > C) causes hemorrhagic cystitis and ____.
questions.exp: S/E I > C: hemorrhagic cystitis, neurotoxicity (Book p283)

questions.q: Mechlorethamine's vesication is prevented by rapid ____.
questions.exp: S/E vesication (prevention: rapid I/V infusion) (Book p283)

questions.q: Melphalan is used for ____.
questions.exp: Melphalan use: multiple myeloma (Book p283)

questions.q: Chlorambucil is used for ____.
questions.exp: Chlorambucil use: chronic lymphocytic leukemia (Book p283)

questions.q: Carmustine, lomustine and semustine treat brain tumors because of good ____ penetration.
questions.exp: Brain tumor (good BBB penetration) (Book p283)

questions.q: The nitrosoureas' side effect is ____.
questions.exp: S/E: neutropenia (Book p283)

questions.q: DOC for pancreatic β-islet cell tumor: ____.
questions.exp: Streptozocin — DOC: pancreatic β-islet cell tumor (Book p283)

questions.q: Dacarbazine and procarbazine (methylation AA agents) are used in ____ ; S/E: MAO inhibition and disulfiram-like reaction.
questions.exp: Use: Hodgkin's disease; S/E MAO inhibition, disulfiram like reaction (Book p283)

questions.q: The methylating AA agent that is DOC for brain tumor is ____.
questions.exp: Temozolomide — DOC: brain tumor (Book p283)

questions.q: Busulfan (use: chronic myeloid leukemia) causes ____ as its S/E.
questions.exp: Busulfan S/E: pulmonary fibrosis (Book p283)

questions.q: Match the platinum fact.
right: Effects like alkylating agents (bind N7 guanine)
questions.exp: Bivalent: cisplatin, carboplatin; quadrivalent: oxaliplatin; effects like alkylating agents (Book p284)

questions.q: Cisplatin nephrotoxicity prevention: 1–2 ltr NS → ____ diuresis (inactivates cisplatin), plus mannitol and amifostine.
questions.exp: Cl- diuresis (inactivates cisplatin) (Book p284)

questions.q: Oxaliplatin (colorectal & pancreatic Ca) has the S/E ____.
questions.exp: S/E: peripheral neuropathy (Book p284)

questions.q: Carboplatin is less toxic than cisplatin but causes ____ suppression.
questions.exp: S/E: bone marrow suppression (Book p284)

questions.q: Anthracycline MOA includes:
opts: Topo-II inhibition (S-phase) + Fe-dependent free radicals (G2-phase); cardiotoxicity prevented by dexrazoxane
Topo-I inhibition (S-phase) with radical-independent cardiotoxicity prevented by amifostine
RNA polymerase inhibition (G2-phase) with nephrotoxicity prevented by mannitol Cl-diuresis
Microtubule stabilization (M-phase) with neuropathy prevented by vitamin B6 supplement
questions.exp: Inhibit topoisomerase-II → S-phase; free radical (needs Fe) → G2-phase; S/E cardiotoxicity; prevention dexrazoxane (Book p284)

questions.q: Match the anthracycline to its use.
questions.exp: Doxorubicin: osteosarcoma, Hodgkin's; idarubicin/daunorubicin + cytarabine: AML; epirubicin: breast; valrubicin: bladder (Book p285)

questions.q: Mitoxantrone is used in multiple sclerosis and ____.
questions.exp: Mitoxantrone: multiple sclerosis, myelogenic leukemia (AML) (Book p285)

questions.q: Red urine is seen with doxorubicin and ____.
questions.exp: Red urine with doxorubicin, daunorubicin (Book p285)

questions.q: Deficiency of ____ hydrolase (responsible for bleomycin metabolism) explains bleomycin's lung and skin toxicity.
questions.exp: Deficiency of bleomycin hydrolase → pulmonary fibrosis, flagellate dermatitis (Book p285)

questions.q: Bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis is due to type-____ pneumocyte damage.
questions.exp: Pulmonary fibrosis (type-II pneumocyte damage) (Book p285)

questions.q: Actinomycin-D/dactinomycin binds to DNA and inhibits ____ polymerase.
questions.exp: Binds to DNA → inhibits RNA polymerase (Book p285)

questions.q: Actinomycin-D is used for choriocarcinoma and ____ tumor.
questions.exp: Use: choriocarcinoma, Wilms tumor (Book p285)

questions.q: Skin turns red when CT follows prior RT in the same area — the ____ syndrome.
questions.exp: Radiation recall syndrome (Book p285)

questions.q: Radiation recall syndrome is seen with:
questions.exp: Seen in: dactinomycin, doxorubicin, daunorubicin (Book p285)

questions.q: Mitomycin-C (topo-II inhibitor, like alkylating agent) has the S/E ____.
questions.exp: S/E: HUS (Book p285)

questions.q: Ocular mitomycin-C prevents ____ scarring; topical prevents synechiae/stenosis in laryngo-tracheal & nasal surgery.
questions.exp: Ocular: prevents corneal scarring (Book p285)

units.title: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma
units.sec: Alkylating Agents: MOA and Secondary Carcinoma · p282
units.guide: Alkyl group devoid of H; binds H on guanine N7; guanine mispairs with thymidine (G≡T). Functional check gates → cytotoxic death; non-functional → proliferation → secondary carcinoma, AML m/c (platinum & AA).

units.title: Nitrogen Mustards
units.guide: Cyclophosphamide prodrug → 4-hydroxy (active); liver splits: phosphoramide mustard (cytotoxic), acrolein (hemorrhagic cystitis, mesna), chloroacetaldehyde (GTCS/ataxia), inactive excreted. Uses female/kids/Wegener's/nephrotic. Ifosfamide I>C cystitis+neuro. Mechlorethamine vesication (rapid IV). Melphalan myeloma; chlorambucil CLL.

units.title: Nitrosoureas, Methylating and Miscellaneous AA
units.sec: Nitrosoureas, Methylating and Miscellaneous AA · p283
units.guide: Nitrosoureas (carmustine/lomustine/semustine): brain tumor (BBB), neutropenia. Streptozocin: pancreatic β-islet DOC. Methylating: dacarbazine/procarbazine Hodgkin's (MAO inhibition, disulfiram-like); temozolomide brain tumor DOC. Busulfan CML, pulmonary fibrosis.

units.title: Platinum Compounds
units.guide: Bivalent cisplatin/carboplatin; quadrivalent oxaliplatin; effects like AA. Cisplatin nephro: NS → Cl- diuresis, mannitol, amifostine. Oxaliplatin colorectal/pancreatic, peripheral neuropathy. Carboplatin less toxic, marrow suppression.

units.title: Anthracyclines
units.guide: Topo-II (S-phase) + Fe-radical (G2-phase); cardiotoxicity (dexrazoxane). Doxorubicin osteosarcoma/Hodgkin's; idarubicin/daunorubicin+cytarabine AML; epirubicin breast; valrubicin bladder; mitoxantrone MS/AML. Red urine doxorubicin/daunorubicin.

units.title: Bleomycin
units.guide: MOA like anthracyclin. Hodgkin's, testicular Ca. Bleomycin hydrolase deficiency → pulmonary fibrosis (type-II pneumocyte) + flagellate dermatitis.

units.title: Actinomycin-D and Mitomycin-C
units.guide: Actinomycin-D binds DNA → inhibits RNA polymerase; choriocarcinoma, Wilms; radiation recall (also doxorubicin/daunorubicin). Mitomycin-C topo-II/AA-like; IV anal Ca, ocular corneal scarring, topical synechiae; S/E HUS.
